photos.question: During surgery under general anesthesia, a client develops muscle rigidity, a rising end-tidal CO2 and a rapidly rising temperature. Which medication should the nurse prepare?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #329!

🔥 The temperature is climbing fast in the OR. What do you grab?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Dantrolene

🧠 Rationale: These are signs of malignant hyperthermia.

Dantrolene relaxes the muscles and stops the runaway heat.

Succinylcholine can trigger it, so it must be stopped.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Malignant Hyperthermia

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Rising end-tidal CO2 (often first)

🔹 Muscle rigidity, jaw tightness

🔹 Fast heart rate, high fever

💊 Triggers:

🔹 Inhaled anesthetic gases

🔹 Succinylcholine

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Stop the trigger agent

✅ Give dantrolene IV

✅ Cool the client, give 100% oxygen

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 Any unexplained rise in CO2 or temperature during anesthesia

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

DANTROLENE puts out the fire!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Pharmacology #Anesthesia #Perioperative #Dantrolene #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client is starting ethambutol for tuberculosis. Which symptom should the client report right away?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #330!

👀 This TB drug can affect one sense. Do you know which?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Blurred vision or trouble seeing red and green

🧠 Rationale: Ethambutol can damage the optic nerve.

Early signs are blurry vision and trouble telling red from green.

Orange urine is expected with rifampin, not ethambutol.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Ethambutol

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 First-line TB medication

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Active tuberculosis, with other TB drugs

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Optic neuritis

🔹 Red-green color changes

🔹 Raised uric acid

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check vision before starting

✅ Repeat eye checks during therapy

✅ Teach to report vision changes fast

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

E for Ethambutol, E for EYES!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client at 7 weeks of pregnancy has sudden sharp pain on one side of the lower abdomen and pain in the shoulder. What should the nurse suspect?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #331!

🚨 Early pregnancy, one-sided pain and shoulder pain. What is going on?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Ruptured ectopic pregnancy

🧠 Rationale: One-sided pain early in pregnancy is a warning sign of ectopic pregnancy.

Shoulder pain suggests bleeding inside the abdomen that irritates the diaphragm.

This is an emergency.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Ectopic Pregnancy

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Sharp one-sided pelvic pain

🔹 Shoulder pain from internal bleeding

🔹 Dizziness, low BP, fast pulse

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check vital signs often

✅ Start IV access, keep NPO

✅ Prepare for surgery or methotrexate

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 Signs of shock: report right away

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Early pregnancy + shoulder pain = think rupture!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Maternity #OBNursing #EctopicPregnancy #Emergency #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: During a first hemodialysis session, a client develops a headache, nausea and restlessness. What should the nurse suspect?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #332!

🧠 First dialysis session and the client feels awful. Why?

This is a HIGH-YIELD renal question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Dialysis disequilibrium syndrome

🧠 Rationale: Urea is removed from the blood faster than from the brain.

Fluid shifts into brain cells and causes swelling.

It is most common during the first sessions.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Dialysis Disequilibrium Syndrome

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Headache, nausea, vomiting

🔹 Restlessness, confusion

🔹 Seizures if severe

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Slow the dialysis rate

✅ Report to the provider

✅ Use shorter first sessions

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 Confusion or seizure activity

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Too FAST a pull = brain SWELL!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Renal #Hemodialysis #Nephrology #CKD #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Parents ask what to do if their 2-year-old has another febrile seizure at home. Which instruction is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #333!

👶 Fever spike and a seizure. What should the parents do?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatrics question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Lay the child on the side, time it

🧠 Rationale: Side-lying keeps the airway open and lets saliva drain.

Timing the seizure helps the provider decide care.

Never put anything in the mouth or hold the child down.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Febrile Seizures

❤️ Who gets them:

🔹 Children 6 months to 5 years

🔹 Often with a fast rising fever

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Stay calm, place child on the side

✅ Move objects away

✅ Time the seizure

🚑 When to escalate:

🔹 Call 911 if it lasts over 5 minutes

🔹 Trouble breathing or blue color

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

SIDE, SAFE, TIME it!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Pediatrics #PedsNursing #FebrileSeizure #Neuro #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: When should the nurse schedule chest physiotherapy for a child with cystic fibrosis?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #334!

🫁 Timing matters with this airway clearance treatment!

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — 1 hour before meals

🧠 Rationale: Chest physiotherapy loosens thick mucus.

Doing it on a full stomach can cause vomiting.

Plan it before meals or 2 hours after.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Chest Physiotherapy

❤️ Purpose:

🔹 Loosen and move thick mucus

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Give bronchodilator first

✅ Do it before meals

✅ Mouth care after

⚠️ Watch for:

🔹 Vomiting if done after eating

🔹 Breathing distress

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

CPT before you EAT!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client is taking metoclopramide for gastroparesis. Which adverse effect should the nurse report?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #335!

👅 This GI drug has a boxed warning. Do you know it?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Involuntary movements of the face or tongue

🧠 Rationale: Metoclopramide can cause tardive dyskinesia.

Signs include lip smacking and tongue movements.

It can be permanent, so stop the drug and report it.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Metoclopramide (Reglan)

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Antiemetic, GI motility drug

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Gastroparesis

🔹 Nausea and vomiting

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Tardive dyskinesia

🔹 Restlessness, drowsiness

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Give 30 minutes before meals

✅ Watch for abnormal movements

✅ Limit use to 12 weeks

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

REGLAN can make you WIGGLE: watch for movements!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!
